subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the members of the Maison Gardiennage

745180101.text: Hmm... the route taken by the attacking force, and their coordination with their supporting flank teams when targeting an enemy stronghold... These aspects must be studied further.

745180102.text: #But what about {NICKNAME}'s unorthodox tactics? They don't seem to make sense at a glance, and yet...

745180105.text: Indeed! As you can see, once the main force has been deployed, it is difficult for them to disengage for a short period of time. This window is when covering the enemy's flanks and cutting off their reinforcements becomes crucial.

745180106.text: But with limited troops, it becomes difficult to decide how many to allocate to the support unit.

745180107.text: Ugh... If we had the numbers, we could downsize the main force. But if we couldn't spare many, we might not even be able to cut the enemy off... Nobody knows for sure how much manpower we'd have each time.

745180108.text: It's customary for the Special Patrol to form a support unit of about one quarter the strength of the main attacking force, and deploy them to patrol areas where we might expect enemy reinforcements to show up...

745180109.text: Normally, this arrangement would suffice, although there have been exceptions... One time, while the support unit was leisurely patrolling their target area with no enemies in sight, the main force was running thin and had to fight for their lives...

745180110.text: But as for you, Proto-Boss — you planned your attack routes for the main force exceptionally well, coordinating their movements with those of the support unit.

745180111.text: That way, both units could rely on each other for support when it mattered, making the most of our manpower.

745180112.text: When the main assault met heavy resistance, the support unit could act like reinforcements. Likewise, when enemy reinforcements suddenly arrived in force, both teams could move in tandem to intercept. Like an offensive-defensive unit!
